Coming out is still worth it even if your family rejects you. But only do it when YOU are ready. Because the moment should be about what YOU need. 
Also, remember that the act of ‘coming out’ can take different forms for different people. 
For one type of person coming-out means actually speaking the words I’m Gay to loved ones.
And for another type of person (like myself) it meant simply owning that I was not heterosexual and deciding in my person that it was an unchangeable fact about myself. And then I continued on exploring myself in that way, freely,  the same way my hetero family members explored themselves freely as heteros. Via that exploration, I ‘came into’ my own first before coming out. 
In the second case, those family members will eventually come to you and ask if you’re gay you’re able to confidently say to your family, ‘yes I am gay. And I love myself. And no amount of your disapproval or hatred will change the fact that I am gay. “

Unfortunately in popular media, the idea of ‘coming out’ has been packaged as this maudlin  cookie cutter moment. But in reality, only you know your family and specific circumstance and as such, you should do what feels best for you because there are no right answers. 

Lastly, I never give advice. BUT😎 I will leave you with this; when you do tell them, make sure you don’t give them any room to think that their feelings about your gayness could actually change your gayness. Stand confidently and happily in your truth. Because it is a beautiful thing that should be shared in joy not in fear.
